newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary to issue 7-yr govt bond for the first time.
newsitem.headline: Hungary to issue 7-yr govt bond for the first time.

text.p: Hungary will issue this month a seven-year government bond, a paper with much longer maturity than government securities issued so far, the Government Debt Managament Agency (AKK) said on Tuesday.
"AKK issues the new bond to increase the average maturity of government papers," the AKK said in a statement.

Most of Hungary's domestic state debt is currently embodied by discount Treasury bills, with up to 12 months maturity, and two- and three-year government bonds. The first issue of the seven-year bond will be auctioned on October 10. @
The interest on the bond will follow the official consumer price index every six months, providing three percent real yield, and will be paid once a year. The starting interest is 25.9 percent.
The low interest rate risk of the bond is likely to make it attractive to institutional investors, mainly insurance companies, the AKK said.
The AKK is likely to offer seven billion forints worth of the new bond at the first auction, some 15 billion forints altogether this year, and plans to continue the issues next year also.
